correctness.rationale: The full biclique projection is a row/column mean projector. The exact Schur complement of the deleted matching coordinates gives the matrix P_{ef}=L/n+O/[n(n-2)]-(n-2+s_e)(n-2+s_f)/[n(n-2)(n(n-2)+t)]. The proof classifies all feasible signs including reverse matching-edge currents, counts all three row sums and bounds the mixed class using (t-1)(n-t-1)<=(n-2)^2/4. The largest norm is realized by an untouched-endpoint row except at full matching deletion, and its sign input attains the bound. The last-drop identity follows by subtraction. The standalone exact rational incidence calculation, independent of the stated kernel, passed 123,977 assertions for n=3..9, all t; finite checks are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The canonical least-squares gradient projector is a physically motivated edge-data reconstruction operator; bounded comparison errors naturally call for its induced coordinatewise norm. Matching deletions model a minimal family of disjoint missing observations. Beyond an exact computation, the classification reveals a strict monotone stability change at every deletion, exact norming-edge types and a terminal jump (n-2)(n+1) times the preceding step. These all-size structural properties are not recovered from a generic matrix identity, the undeleted projector norm, or trace-only resistance statistics. The result is relevant to endpoint robustness of incomplete comparison networks without asserting broader applications not demonstrated.
